builder_plan.scenario: An agent reads external documents or tool responses that may contain malicious instructions.
builder_plan.change: Replay attacks and legitimate lookalikes in an isolated copy of your agent workflow.
builder_plan.baseline: Your existing checks with the same tasks, permissions, and tool responses.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Successful attacks missed, legitimate actions blocked, detection delay, and review cost.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: When Safety Rationales Hallucinate: Diagnosing and Grounding Multimodal Safety Guards
summary: TCG-RL replaces outcome-only supervised or preference training of rationale-generating safety guards with a contrastive RL objective that rewards tool use only when it improves grounding over a tool-free reference. It costs an RL training pipeline (reward computation against a tool-free baseline, tool-execution environment) rather than simple fine-tuning, increasing training complexity and compute beyond what one 24 GB GPU comfortably supports. It can fail if the tool-free reference is a weak comparator, if tool coverage does not match the fine-grained attributes and relations where hallucination concentrates, or if grounding rewards degrade classification calibration.
rationale: The diagnosis (rationales hallucinate regardless of scale or accuracy) is directly actionable for anyone deploying multimodal safety guards, but adopting TCG-RL itself requires reinforcement-learning training infrastructure and a tool-use environment that strain a single 24 GB GPU.
technique: Tool-Contrastive Grounding RL for safety rationales

claims.statement: TCG-RL replaces outcome-only supervised or preference training of rationale-generating safety guards with a contrastive RL objective that rewards tool use only when it improves grounding over a tool-free reference. It costs an RL training pipeline (reward computation against a tool-free baseline, tool-execution environment) rather than simple fine-tuning, increasing training complexity and compute beyond what one 24 GB GPU comfortably supports. It can fail if the tool-free reference is a weak comparator, if tool coverage does not match the fine-grained attributes and relations where hallucination concentrates, or if grounding rewards degrade classification calibration.
TCG-RL substantially reduces rationale hallucination while maintaining competitive safety prediction performance (no numeric factor reported in the abstract).
